title: Paradox Bloom
logline: BaneWAP seizes the egg and wishes huge — and the wish grants at once, minimum-viable, an empire hollow as a rented crown.
epigraph: A grand wish grants easily. It is the finishing that never comes.
description: Chapter 11 of Lore.Land: Paradox Bloom. BaneWAP snatches the unspent wish and wishes an empire; karmic momentum obliges one coincidence at a time, delivering it mediocre and hollow. Bloom arrives before seed, his hoarded berries wake inside him, and the egg — unfinished, unfinishable — rolls back warm to Boof's paws.

content.text: It happened between one honest sniff and the next. On the road out of Bone.land, where the audit still hung fresh in the air, Mr. BaneWAP stopped shadowing and simply took — banker's crust cracking with the effort, tin lockbox open and shut, the egg gone from Boof's sling before her growl could finish forming. He did not run far. He did not need to. He stood on a low rise with the warm shell in both crimped hands and wished the wish he had been drafting since the auction failed: an empire, whole, at once. And the wish — this is the part no one had priced — granted instantly. It was a moment of

children.text: . Karmic momentum does not refuse a grand wish. It simply pays it out the way momentum pays everything: one coincidence at a time, minimum-viable, corrections deferred. A barn deed blew against his crust. A road bent to end at his feet. A distant clerk misfiled a fortune in his name. The empire arrived. It arrived mediocre.

content.text: His empire arrived in pieces: throne first, banners after, subjects caught halfway through errands. One still held a loaf. The throne smelled rented. The banners hung in colors nobody had ordered. Boof watched the new emperor wait for the scene to feel complete. It kept arriving. It never did.

content.text: Deep beneath his crust, a berry woke. The wish had passed through him, leaving its drop of light just as it had in the fields. One seam shone, then another. Warmth worked through the bitter filling. He tasted what he had kept from everyone, himself included. Sweet. It had been sweet all along. Around him, the banners stirred. He made a small sound the throne did nothing to support.

content.text: The Midas touch, sampled: everything he grasped turned to more, and none of it to enough. Sound it, send it back sweeter. That is the whole law.
He tapped the rented throne once — hollow — and let the note say what the audit had: interest is owed on every borrowed want.

sections.title: The Wish That Would Not Finish

content.text: Here is the paradox the audit had circled without naming: a wish only leaves its shell when it is finished, and a wish the size of an empire is never finishable. There is always one more coincidence owed, one more correction pending in some far county where a stranger's luck must be bent to balance a king's. The grant kept arriving and kept not being done. The empire stood, hollow as a rented crown, and the egg in BaneWAP's hands stayed exactly as warm as it had been in the frozen furrow — spent and unspent at once, a note held but not released. At the edge of the new court, a woman still holding her market basket asked whether she could go home. A banner brushed her shoulder. No one answered; the emperor was staring at his own hands. Boof could smell bread cooling in the basket and dust rising where the throne had scraped the ground. The empire needed this woman to be a subject. She needed to get the bread indoors before rain. Boof watched her take one step backward, then another. The banner lifted, and she slipped beneath it.

His crimped hands softened. The egg slipped, tipped, rolled down the rise, past a banner dragging in the dust. Boof stepped forward. It came to rest against her paws, warm as ever. The crack had widened enough to show gold within. She checked the shell with her nose. Still humming. Still waiting.

content.text: Eight honks sounded. The ninth still sleeps in the shell. Small wishes travel farthest.
He pointed downhill to two rivers that had not yet agreed to forget their springs, and Boof — who finally almost knew her want — went to meet them.

loreItems.description: A grand wish grants instantly and minimum-viable: karmic momentum pays it out one coincidence at a time, corrections deferred elsewhere.
A wish only leaves the shell when it is finished. An empire-sized wish is never finishable, so the egg survives its own spending and rolls home.
BaneWAP's hoarded berries wake inside him — a berry notices the story it is sitting inside — and he tastes his hoard for the first time in years. Sweetness is the correction.
